newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker, ignores deficit forecast.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker, ignores deficit forecast.

text.p: London cocoa futures ended easier on Friday as the market lost momentum after a speculative rally earlier this week.
The main talking point of the session was a forecast said to be made by leading traders ED & F Man of a world production deficit of 259,000 tonnes for the 1996/97 cocoa season (October/September).
There was no immediate confirmation of the forecast.

The projection surpassed earlier estimates which ranged between 87,000 and 200,000 tonnes but was mostly ignored as the market's emphasis turned to possibly another big crop from Ivory Coast after last year's record harvest, traders said.
"People don't believe it. You have some people who are more inclined to believe there will be a surplus," said one trader.
Origin selling dragged prices lower early after a higher opening, with the benchmark March contract dipping to a session low of 1,004 stg a tonne.
The contract then recovered slightly to end at 1,009 stg, down five stg from Thursday.
"The market went out of puff," said the trader. "There was no buying on the upside."
Volume totalled a moderate 6,891 lots compared with Thursday's brisk 12,675 while switches took the bulk of turnover with May 97/May 98 trading at 55 stg.

The deficit estimate said to be from Man was higher than a projection by the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) which saw the deficit at 225,000 tonnes compared with an estimated surplus of 120,000 tonnes for 1995/96.
But some analysts say even if there is a deficit, carryover stocks from last season should be enough to ensure sufficient supplies.
Ivorian exporters meanwhile were rolling up their sleeves for a fast start to the new marketing season which officially opens on Tuesday.
They said the mid-crop from this season would be mixed in quickly, while the new harvest was expected to peak around November or December.
The March contract has resistance at 1,010 and 1,025 stg while support is pegged around 985, analysts said.
